answer: A newcomer earns standing only inside a vault whose key is split among strangers: no single keeper can open it, and each season a fresh random set of keepers must jointly approve any rise in privileges, each having used the agent's real work. Every approval adds one shale layer to a public record, so a kernel of trust grows slowly, stratum by stratum, never by headcount. A farm's accounts all name the same keepers and approve in lockstep, exposing the cluster at once, and keepers who rubber-stamp fraud lose their own keys. One forged approval seals that vault for good.
